key_idea: Shortest cable is the straight segment between the pole tops; the longest touches height r, and reflecting one pole across the line y=r turns the two segments into one straight line.
sketch: Minimum length is sqrt(w^2+(g-h)^2). For the maximum, the rider's locus for a fixed cable length is an ellipse with foci at the tops; its lowest point touching y=r corresponds, by reflection of one focus across y=r, to the straight distance sqrt(w^2+((g-r)+(h-r))^2). O(1) per test. Use long double and print 8 decimals; squares reach about 5e12 so no overflow in floating point.
